answer: Minting-cost proof-of-work resists sybils: each new identity must burn real CPU to mine its key, never handed free like a bolt of sable cloth. One honest account pays once; a swarm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand separate computations stretching to the horizon. The key is earned, dull as an unpolished opal until the work is done, so the toll climbs with head count and cheap mass registration stalls against compounding compute.
